$comment:
Camera framing: how far the view looks down a steep slope. Feature 008 (specs/008-reaction-time-speed). Read by the renderer only, never by the simulation, so no value here can change a run or a score. It does change how much time a player has to see what is coming, which is feel - so it lives in data like tuning does (Principle III), and a changed value goes to the play pass like a course edit does (Principle VIII).

Why the camera looks down at all. It holds the skier 60% of the way down a 180-tall frame, which leaves 72 units below him. On ground steeper than about 0.41, the piste 213 units ahead - the whole of the horizontal lookahead every device is promised - is more than 72 below him, so a log was still under the bottom edge when it was close enough to see. On the Narrows that cost a player up to a third of the time the lookahead was supposed to buy. The camera now drops just far enough to show the piste across that full 213 units, and no further; it never shows more than today in the air, where the booters already use the headroom.

lookMargin: how far inside the bottom edge the piste 213 units ahead is kept, so a whole log is on screen and not just its top pixel.

shelfMargin: riding the piste under an upper shelf, its top edge is kept at least this far inside the top of the frame. Without it the look-down pushes the final shelf to the frame edge at the finish line; the shelf reading as a choice outranks seeing a little further down.

shelfEaseIn: the distance before a shelf over which that cap blends in, so the camera never snaps as a shelf arrives.
